title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a suffix-free letter table with word-end reading and right-quotient capacity
summary: A fixed small letter code may be suffix-free without being prefix-free. The writer concatenates codes in ordinary source-letter order; the reader identifies them from the visible word end and restores their source order. Reversing working-unit sequences converts the class exactly into a prefix-code problem, so complete-word right quotients and dual branch counts give necessary capacity bounds. This is a new orientation-specific proposal in the reviewed workflow, not new coding theory, a native reading, an executed count or a completed historical writer.

contract.working_alphabet: A fixed finite alphabet A of working units; the contemplated limit is22. Multi-ASCII labels such as ch or cph designate single elements only if that unit binding is explicitly adopted. Their native atomicity is not established here.
contract.source_alphabet: A fixed finite source alphabet Sigma with at most22 distinct characters for this proposed small-table class. Each source character has exactly one distinct nonempty codeword over A. No source language or character value is selected here.
contract.codebook: C is finite and suffix-free: no distinct codeword is a proper suffix of another. Lengths may be any positive finite integers. Codes can share initial units; distinct long codes can also share terminal units as long as neither is a suffix of the other.
contract.word_contract: Each complete source word is written as the concatenation of its character codes in unchanged source order. Visible source-word spaces and paragraph boundaries remain visible. No code crosses a whole-word boundary; no empty code, optional alias, context state, padding or erased character is allowed.
contract.nontriviality: At least one codeword longer than one working unit must actually be used in the parse of an observed complete group. Unused long entries do not qualify.
contract.identity_exception: C=A always writes every group over A with singleton codes and at most22 entries. A bound above22 can concern only the declared actually-used multi-unit condition, never all suffix-free codes.
contract.physical_scope: This is a formal complete-word channel and necessary-condition proposal. A later actual writer must bind a source alphabet, a table, punctuation and a finite physical line contract. Unknown names are spellable only from the declared source alphabet; outside characters are rejected, not silently normalized. Punctuation either consumes declared source-character entries or needs a separately paid visible convention. Words are not allowed to split invisibly over a line; until continuation is specified, only unbroken words fitting the physical line are covered.

writing: Keep the ordinary source-word sequence and character order.
For each character, copy its fixed table entry in the table's stated orientation.
Concatenate those entries within the word and write the source-word space. No hidden internal boundary marker is supplied.
reading: Locate a visible complete word end.
Read working units leftward until a table entry ending there is identified. Suffix-freeness ensures no shorter or longer rival code ends at that same position.
Remove that code and repeat on the remaining prefix until the complete group is consumed. A stuck nonempty remainder is invalid.

The recovered source characters arrive last first. Put them into their original order, for example by writing them right-to-left into a scratch word slot, then read the reconstructed source word normally. Keep the visible sequence of words unchanged.
hand_procedure.costs: The reader learns every character/code pairing, the total sum of code lengths, and the end-first lookup rule. Reading needs word-local reverse-order handling or a scratch line; it is not as immediate as ordinary left-to-right letter reading. Normal source-language knowledge is still necessary. No whole-word meanings, private message IDs or dictionary of target forms is provided.
hand_procedure.historical_status: A modern teachable construction and mathematical class; no historical attestation, native writing direction or reversed plaintext claim.

unit_reversal_equivalence.definition: rho reverses the ordered list of working units in one string. For a tuple (ch,o,cfh), rho gives (cfh,o,ch), never the character reversal of the printed label cho cfh.
unit_reversal_equivalence.code_property: C is suffix-free if and only if rho(C) is prefix-free; codebook size and every code length are unchanged.
unit_reversal_equivalence.word_property: w=c1...cn lies in C* if and only if rho(w)=rho(cn)...rho(c1) lies in rho(C)*. The used-multi-unit property is also preserved.
unit_reversal_equivalence.limit: This is an exact mathematical reduction on fixed unit sequences. It does not claim the original manuscript, writer, source language or whole paragraph ran backwards. A result on W is not automatically a result on rho(W); the transformed complete groups are a different predeclared input to the dual argument.

right_quotient_theorem.statement: If u and v=r u both lie in C* for suffix-free C, then r lies in C*.
right_quotient_theorem.direct_proof: Both strings must have the same last codeword: two possible last codes are suffix-comparable, hence equal by suffix-freeness. Repeated cancellation consumes exactly the known complete code sequence for u from the end of v. The remaining prefix r therefore ends at a true code boundary and is a concatenation of complete codes.
right_quotient_theorem.reversal_proof: rho(v)=rho(u)rho(r). Apply the prefix-quotient theorem to rho(C), then reverse back.
right_quotient_theorem.closure: Start R=W and repeatedly add each nonempty r whenever u and r u are already in R. Every resulting string lies in C* and is a prefix of an original word. The closure is finite without imposing a maximum code length.
right_quotient_theorem.singleton: If the one-unit string g is in R, singleton g is an actual codeword. Suffix-freeness then forbids any longer code ending in g.
right_quotient_theorem.not_a_native_word_claim: A derived prefix is a complete code string under this contract, not a newly attested standalone manuscript word or a known source-language word.
right_quotient_theorem.wrong_side_counterexample: C={a,ab} is suffix-free. The strings a and ab are legal, but deleting the complete LEFT prefix a from ab leaves b, which is not in C*. Left cancellation is therefore not licensed for this class.
right_quotient_theorem.mere_UD_counterexample: C={a,ba} is prefix-free and hence freely uniquely decodable, but it is not suffix-free. Both a and ba are legal, whereas the right quotient b is not. Thus the right-quotient implication does not hold for arbitrary UD codes.
right_quotient_theorem.grammar_limit: A code may be readable only after restricting legal source strings or using grammar, despite failing free UD. That is a different contract. For example A->a, B->aa is unambiguous if the only allowed source words are the single letters A and B, but unrestricted source AA collides with B. No such source-language restriction can be imported here as an uncharged substitute for suffix-freeness.

definitions.H: Terminal units of all nonempty strings in the right-quotient closure R.
definitions.F: Units whose singleton strings occur in R; F is a subset of H.
definitions.T: For each exactly two-unit string ab in R, add the directed edge b->a.
definitions.d_h: Number of distinct penultimate units among R strings of length at least2 ending in h.
definitions.candidate_g: Terminal unit of an actually used multi-unit code. Consider every unit occurring anywhere in W, including g not in H.
definitions.N_g: g together with every vertex that reaches g along directed edges of T.

dual_necessary_capacity.basic: |C|>=|H|, because different required terminal units need different codewords.
dual_necessary_capacity.propagation: For ab in R, singleton b implies singleton a by the right quotient. Contrapositively, if a is non-singleton then b is non-singleton. A used long code ending g excludes singleton g, so every h in N_g is non-singleton.
dual_necessary_capacity.impossible_candidate: N_g intersect F nonempty contradicts that candidate. If R is fully closed, F is already forward-closed under T, so for g not in F this extra test is redundant but remains a useful consistency check.
dual_necessary_capacity.branch_obligation: If singleton h is forbidden, two legal strings ending in h with different penultimate units need different h-ending codes. Hence at least max(1,d_h) codes ending in h are needed. The1 covers an actually used g outside H.
dual_necessary_capacity.first_bound: For a possible candidate g: |C|>=|H union {g}|+max(1,d_g)-1.
dual_necessary_capacity.propagated_bound: For a possible candidate g: |C|>=|K_g|+sum over h in N_g of (max(1,d_h)-1). Proper predecessors belong to H because they terminate an R two-unit string; therefore N_g is contained in K_g and no terminal-class contribution is double-counted.
dual_necessary_capacity.global_bound: Take the minimum over all possible actually-used multi-unit terminal candidates g. If none remain, only singleton usage is possible. If the minimum exceeds22, the declared small nontrivial suffix-free class is excluded. A bound at most22 is only NOT EXCLUDED; it does not prove existence, exact minimality, a key or a language.
dual_necessary_capacity.no_presumed_number: No native bound is computed or predicted here. Neither23nor any earlier prefix-side number is assumed.

small_hand_examples.purpose: Positive suffix-free but non-prefix-free hand reading
end_first_steps: Reverse the recovered list [A,B] to source order [B,A].
small_hand_examples.qualification: A and B are merely invented source-character names; no native value or meaningful-language claim is attached to this two-letter example.

small_hand_examples.purpose: Multiple codes may share a terminal unit
small_hand_examples.reason: Suffix-free: a ends neither ab nor cb, and the two b-ending codes are equal length and different. This is not the one-code-per-terminal special case.
Removing the complete suffix a from ba and ca forces singleton b and c. Singleton a,b,c then forbid every used longer code ending in the observed alphabet.

small_hand_examples.purpose: Sharp nontrivial size can exceed identity size
small_hand_examples.proof: If either singleton occurs, the two-unit whole strings force the other singleton by right cancellation, so no used longer code remains possible. Otherwise every length2 word must itself be a code. Thus the exact nontrivial minimum is4 for this toy set, while identity uses2.

known_form_and_statistical_obligations.repeats: No state changes between words: identical whole words and triples are legal whenever the underlying repeated source word is legal. If X is a legal code string, XX is legal too. This gives formal capacity only, not a semantic assignment or predicted frequency.
known_form_and_statistical_obligations.diversity: There is no fixed three-unit interior alphabet or six-terminal-role table. This does not prove compatibility with any known long or short native group.
known_form_and_statistical_obligations.q_and_y: No privileged q/o transition or y-ending rule is introduced. Their known statistical obligations remain entirely unaddressed by free decoding alone.
known_form_and_statistical_obligations.word_statistics: With one fixed injective letter code and preserved source-word spaces, distinct source words remain distinct output groups, so word types and complete-word equality frequencies are preserved. Prior source-specific word-frequency exclusions therefore still apply when their same source/input assumptions are adopted. This proposal is not a rescue of those writers.
